recipe.title: Blackberry, Skyr & Jumbo Oat Overnight Pots with Chia and Toasted Walnuts
recipe.description: High-protein overnight pots combining creamy plain skyr, chewy jumbo oats and chia with a sharp-sweet crushed blackberry and lemon ripple, finished with fresh blackberries and walnuts toasted immediately before serving for aromatic crunch.

ingredients.purchase_quantity: Buy: 1 tub containing at least 400 g
ingredients.purchase_notes: Plain, unsweetened skyr. Exact tub size varies by retailer; any pack providing at least 400 g is suitable.
ingredients.notes: Use: 400 g. Plain high-protein skyr provides the principal protein component and the creamy base.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Choose jumbo rolled oats rather than instant or finely milled porridge oats for better overnight texture.

ingredients.purchase_quantity: Buy: enough punnets to provide at least 180 g
ingredients.purchase_notes: Punnet sizes vary. Select ripe but intact berries without visible mould or leaking juice.
ingredients.preparation: Wash gently in cold water and dry thoroughly. Allocate 120 g to the blackberry ripple and reserve 60 g whole for serving.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Any standard fresh semi-skimmed cow's milk is suitable.
Pack size is not critical provided at least 20 g is available.
Use plain, unsalted walnuts. Pack size is not critical.
ingredients.preparation: Inspect for shell fragments, then roughly chop into pieces approximately 5-8 mm across before toasting.
ingredients.notes: Use: 20 g total, approximately 10 g per serving.

ingredients.purchase_notes: A mild-flavoured clear or runny honey is preferred so the blackberry flavour remains dominant.
ingredients.notes: Use: 12 g. The quantity is intentionally restrained; the berries should retain noticeable acidity.

ingredients.purchase_notes: An unwaxed lemon is preferable because the zest is used.
ingredients.preparation: Wash and dry. Finely grate approximately 2 g yellow zest without removing the white pith. Cut the lemon and squeeze 10 ml juice. Reserve the remainder for another use.
ingredients.notes: Recipe use is approximately 2 g zest plus 10 ml juice; the whole fruit is purchased.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use vanilla extract rather than artificial vanilla essence where available.
Fine table or fine sea salt is suitable.
ingredients.notes: Use: 0.125 tsp. This small quantity sharpens the dairy, oat and berry flavours without making the finished breakfast taste salty.

equipment.notes: Required for accurate ingredient quantities and even portioning.
For measuring the milk and lemon juice.
For combining the overnight oat base.
For removing fine lemon zest without excessive white pith.
For cutting the lemon and chopping the walnuts.
For dry-toasting the walnuts immediately before serving.
Used only for controlled walnut toasting.

equipment.display_name: 2 individual lidded breakfast pots or containers
equipment.notes: Each container should comfortably hold at least 400 ml.

mise_en_place.instruction: Place the as-bought blackberries in a colander or sieve. Rinse gently under cold running water without crushing them. Drain, spread on clean kitchen paper or a clean cloth and dry thoroughly. Weigh 120 g into the small bowl for the ripple and reserve 60 g intact in a covered refrigerated container for serving.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The berries are clean and dry, with 120 g allocated to the ripple and 60 g reserved whole.

mise_en_place.instruction: Wash and dry the whole lemon. Using the fine grater, remove approximately 2 g of the yellow outer zest only; stop before exposing significant white pith. Cut the lemon in half on the chopping board and squeeze 10 ml juice into the measuring jug, removing any seeds. Reserve the unused lemon for another purpose.
mise_en_place.endpoint: Approximately 2 g fine yellow zest and exactly 10 ml lemon juice are ready for use, with no seeds or large pieces of pith.

mise_en_place.instruction: Inspect the walnuts for shell fragments and discard any found. Using the chef's knife, roughly chop the walnuts into approximately 5-8 mm pieces. Do not toast yet.
mise_en_place.endpoint: 20 g walnuts are evenly chopped into coarse pieces suitable for dry-toasting.

mise_en_place.instruction: Weigh 100 g jumbo oats, 400 g skyr, 20 g chia seeds and 12 g honey. Measure 150 ml semi-skimmed milk, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 0.5 tsp ground cinnamon and 0.125 tsp fine salt. Keep chilled ingredients refrigerated until immediately before assembly.
mise_en_place.endpoint: All ingredients are accurately measured and ready for immediate assembly.

procedure.title: Crush and season the blackberry ripple
procedure.instruction: Place the allocated 120 g blackberries in the small bowl. Add all 12 g honey, the prepared 10 ml lemon juice and approximately 2 g lemon zest. Using the back of a spoon, press and stir the berries until approximately two-thirds of the fruit has broken down while visible small berry pieces remain. Continue stirring until the honey is completely dispersed.
procedure.endpoint: The mixture is glossy and spoonable with released purple juice, no concentrated streaks of honey and some identifiable blackberry pieces remaining.

corrective_actions.condition: The mixture remains mostly whole and does not release enough juice to form a ripple.
corrective_actions.action: Continue pressing the berries firmly against the side of the bowl in 20-second intervals until sufficient juice is released.
Do not process further; retain the mixture as made. The flavour remains acceptable, although the intended fruit-piece texture will be reduced.

procedure.title: Combine the skyr, oats and chia base
procedure.instruction: Add 400 g skyr and 150 ml semi-skimmed milk to the mixing bowl and stir until uniformly loosened. Add 100 g jumbo oats, 20 g chia seeds, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 0.5 tsp ground cinnamon and 0.125 tsp fine salt. Fold and stir thoroughly, scraping the base and sides of the bowl, until every visible oat flake and chia seed is coated and no dry pockets remain.
procedure.endpoint: The mixture is thick but readily spoonable, homogeneous except for visible oats and chia, with no dry clumps or unmixed skyr.

corrective_actions.condition: Dry oats or chia remain trapped at the base or sides of the bowl.
corrective_actions.action: Scrape the affected area and fold repeatedly until all dry material is completely incorporated.

corrective_actions.condition: The mixture appears unusually loose immediately after mixing.
corrective_actions.action: Proceed without adding additional oats; chia and oats will absorb liquid during refrigeration.

procedure.title: Layer the overnight pots
procedure.instruction: Place the first lidded container on the kitchen scales and tare. Add approximately one-quarter of the oat mixture, followed by approximately one-quarter of the blackberry ripple. Repeat once in the same container. Repeat the complete operation with the second container so that both pots receive equal quantities. Use a spoon to make one or two shallow folds through each pot, producing visible blackberry streaks without fully homogenising the colour. Fit the lids immediately.
procedure.endpoint: Both containers contain approximately equal portions with distinct purple blackberry ripples distributed through the pale oat-skyr base.

corrective_actions.condition: One pot is visibly heavier than the other.
corrective_actions.action: Use the scales to transfer small amounts between containers until the total filled weights are approximately equal.

corrective_actions.condition: The blackberry ripple has been fully mixed in and no streaking remains.
corrective_actions.action: Do not continue mixing. Flavour will remain correct; only the intended visual contrast will be reduced.

procedure.title: Refrigerate until fully hydrated
procedure.instruction: Transfer the sealed containers immediately to a refrigerator operating at 5°C or below. Refrigerate undisturbed for a minimum of 8 hours and preferably overnight. Do not proceed to final service until the oats and chia have hydrated sufficiently to produce a cohesive spoonable texture.
procedure.endpoint: The jumbo oats are tender while retaining gentle chew, the chia is fully hydrated without dry seed clusters, and no free pool of milk remains at the base of either container.

corrective_actions.condition: A small amount of free liquid remains visible after 8 hours.
corrective_actions.action: Stir the pot thoroughly and refrigerate for an additional 30-60 minutes before serving.

corrective_actions.condition: Dry chia or oat clusters remain after refrigeration.
corrective_actions.action: Break the clusters apart thoroughly with a spoon and allow a further 30 minutes of refrigerated hydration.

procedure.title: Dry-toast the walnuts
procedure.instruction: Place the dry frying pan over a low-to-medium gas flame. Add the prepared 20 g chopped walnuts in a single layer. Toast while shaking or stirring the pan every 15-20 seconds so the pieces colour evenly.
procedure.endpoint: The walnuts smell distinctly nutty, appear slightly deeper golden-brown than when raw and are hot throughout, with no blackened edges or acrid aroma.

corrective_actions.condition: The walnuts begin darkening rapidly or produce smoke.
corrective_actions.action: Immediately remove the pan from the heat, transfer the walnuts to a cool plate and discard any visibly blackened pieces.

corrective_actions.condition: Little aroma or colour develops after 5 minutes.
corrective_actions.action: Increase the flame slightly and continue in 30-second intervals while stirring continuously until the stated endpoint is reached.

procedure.title: Check texture and finish the pots
procedure.instruction: Remove the overnight pots from the refrigerator. Stir each pot from the bottom upward exactly 2-3 times to redistribute any minor settling while retaining visible blackberry marbling. Divide the reserved 60 g whole blackberries equally between the two pots, approximately 30 g each. Divide the freshly toasted 20 g walnuts equally over the surface, approximately 10 g each. Serve immediately so the walnuts remain crisp.
procedure.endpoint: Each serving is creamy and spoonable with tender-chewy oats, visible blackberry streaks, fresh whole berries and warm or room-temperature crisp toasted walnuts on top.

corrective_actions.condition: The oat mixture has become unevenly compacted during refrigeration.
corrective_actions.action: Fold gently from the base upward until the texture becomes uniform; do not aggressively beat the mixture.

corrective_actions.condition: Condensation or berry juice has accumulated visibly on the surface.
corrective_actions.action: Fold it gently into the oat mixture before adding the fresh blackberry and walnut garnish.

plating.instruction: Serve one chilled pot per person. Keep the fresh blackberries concentrated toward the centre and scatter the toasted walnut pieces across the top so every spoonful can include contrasting creamy, juicy and crunchy elements.

storage.storage_instructions: The assembled oat, skyr and blackberry mixture may be stored sealed at 5°C or below for up to 2 days. For the best texture, keep the 60 g serving blackberries and the un-toasted walnuts separate until required. Toast the walnuts immediately before serving. Do not leave the finished pots at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

either_retailer: Plain 0% skyr: buy at least 400 g
Jumbo rolled oats: buy 1 standard bag
Fresh blackberries: buy enough punnets to provide at least 180 g
Semi-skimmed milk: buy 1 bottle or carton
Runny honey: buy 1 jar or bottle

restaurant_quality_features: A separately prepared blackberry, honey and lemon ripple gives sharper fruit definition than simply mixing whole berries into the oats.
Lemon zest and juice reinforce the natural blackberry acidity and prevent the dairy-oat base tasting flat.
Vanilla, cinnamon and a measured amount of fine salt deepen perceived sweetness without requiring excessive added sugar.
Jumbo oats are used for deliberate tender-chewy texture rather than a homogeneous porridge consistency.
Walnuts are toasted immediately before serving to maximise aromatic flavour and preserve crisp contrast against the chilled creamy base.
Fresh reserved blackberries provide a second fruit texture in addition to the crushed overnight ripple.
nutrition_notes: Estimated nutrition represents one complete serving including honey, milk, chia seeds, walnuts and all garnishes.
Plain skyr provides the majority of the protein while keeping saturated fat relatively low.
Oats, chia seeds, blackberries and walnuts provide substantial dietary fibre.
Added honey is deliberately limited because ripe blackberries, dairy and vanilla already provide perceived sweetness.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary with the exact skyr, milk, oat and walnut products purchased.
critical_success_factors: Use jumbo rolled oats rather than instant oats so the overnight texture remains distinct rather than pasty.
Thoroughly disperse chia seeds before refrigeration; dry clumps will not hydrate evenly.
Allow at least 8 hours of refrigerated hydration before serving.
Keep the reserved serving berries dry to prevent unnecessary surface dilution.
Do not toast the walnuts in advance if maximum crunch is required.
Remove the walnuts from the heat as soon as they become aromatic and lightly browned because their high oil content makes the transition from toasted to burnt rapid.
